SK3541 The HttpClient is disposed at the end of the call

A using owns a directly constructed HttpClient, so the connection pool underneath it is closed once per call.

CategoryLifetime
Default severitywarning
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since2.0

Why

HttpClient is the one disposable in the framework whose correct lifetime is the opposite of every other one's. Disposing it closes the connection pool it holds, and the sockets sit in TIME_WAIT for the operating system's timeout afterwards — so a handler called under load exhausts the ephemeral port range and starts failing with SocketException on a call that worked yesterday, on a machine that is not the author's. ⚠ The whole family this rule lives in says "this is not disposed" and this one says "this is disposed". SK3501, SK3502, SK3530 and SK3532 each report a release that is missing; here the release is present, is what the shape of every other disposable asks for, and is the defect. That inversion is why it cannot be an exception inside one of theirs.

Example

Instead of:

static async Task<string> Fetch(string url) {
    using var client = new HttpClient();
    return await client.GetStringAsync(url);
}

Write:

static readonly HttpClient Client = new();

static async Task<string> Fetch(string url) {
    return await Client.GetStringAsync(url);
}

When it does not fire

⚠ What is proved is the declaration, not the lifetime. The rule speaks only where the using is the thing that ends the client's life — a using statement or a using declaration whose resource is a direct new HttpClient(…). A client assigned to a field, returned, or handed to something else has a lifetime this rule cannot read, and it does not guess at one. ⚠ An entry point is excluded, because a client disposed once for the process is not a client disposed per call; the test is the declaration's own shape — a static Main, or a top-level statement — rather than Compilation.GetEntryPoint, since the same source compiled as a library has no entry point and is the same decision. ⚠ A constructor taking an `HttpMessageHandler` is excluded and that is the important one: new HttpClient(sharedHandler, disposeHandler: false) is the documented mitigation, the sockets belong to the handler, and disposing the thin wrapper above it costs nothing. Without this exclusion the rule would report the fix. ⚠ The canonical correct form — a static readonly field — never reaches the rule at all, because it is not a using. ⚠ Not hosted: measured outside this repository with an empty Directory.Build.props above it, AnalysisMode=All produced no CA diagnostic of any severity on the shape, hidden included. CA2234 fires on the same lines and is about the Uri overload. ⚠ Fixless, and not for want of an edit. The repair is a static readonly client, a constructor-injected one, or IHttpClientFactory — a decision about where this type gets its dependencies, taken at the type or at the container. Deleting the using in place would turn a bounded leak into an unbounded one, which is the one edit a fixing tool must not make on its own.
